eyebrow: Python for Data Engineers · Chapter 5, Lesson 31
subtitle: All or nothing -- and a safe pattern to reuse.

code:
try:
    cursor.execute("TRUNCATE TABLE Staging.ProductSnapshot;")
    cursor.executemany(
        "INSERT INTO Staging.ProductSnapshot "
        "(ProductName, Quantity, UnitPrice) VALUES (?, ?, ?);",
        [("Trail Runner GTX", 2, 129.99), ("Alpine 2P Tent", 1, 249.50)]
    )
    conn.commit()
except pyodbc.Error as err:
    conn.rollback()
    print(f"Load failed, rolled back: {err}")
finally:
    conn.close()
caption: A failed executemany() rolls back the TRUNCATE too -- the table ends up exactly as it started.
Specific exception first, general exception second, re-raise what you don't expect.
